comment: Cycloalkene handler stereo fixtures (BL-03 gap closure, 2026-05-03). All entries are sourced from real benchmark CSV rows per D-23. Phase 152 wires the chain-fragment fallback (composer.py:1808) through the predicate-first injector when features.ring_type == 'cycloalkene'. Per D-10 the existing ring-strain filter at rules/stereochemistry.py:85-92 suppresses E/Z descriptors for ring double bonds in rings < 8 members; ring-atom R/S is unaffected. NOTE: the cycloalkene corpus in opsin_selftest_500.csv provides 4 real candidates (2 with stereo, 2 without), so 2 entries below are no-stereo control compounds (the P-91 pattern matches the bare cycloalkene name; the OPSIN round-trip confirms the handler produces the canonical form). Per BL-03 closure rationale: 4 D-23-compliant fixtures (2 with stereo, 2 controls) is sufficient — the prior count of 6 was inflated by 4 corpus-violating entries. Duplicate-pin alternative was rejected because pytest parametrize IDs would collide on (source_corpus, source_id).

compounds.comment: (4S,5R)-4,5-dihydroxy-3-propylcyclopent-2-en-1-one — ring-atom R/S on cyclopentenone. Real opsin_selftest_500.csv row.
(1R,2S,3S,4R)-cyclohex-5-ene-1,2,3,4-tetraol (conduritol-related) — multi-center R/S on a cyclohexene. Real opsin_selftest_500.csv row.

1,6-dimethylcyclohexene — no stereo; control fixture confirming the cycloalkene Tier-A path produces the bare canonical name when needs_stereo_injection returns False (BL-04 fix gap closure: this fixture EXECUTES non-xfail through the entire pipeline).
4-(buta-1,3-dien-2-yl)-1,5,5-trimethylcyclopentene — no stereo; control fixture. Second non-xfail entry per BL-04 (need >=2 cases that reach OPSIN round-trip step).
